procedural_history.impugned_order: Order of the learned Single Judge of the Bombay High Court at its Nagpur Bench dated 18 August 2016, which allowed a criminal application filed by the respondent and issued a direction for the de-freezing of his bank accounts.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings:
1. Initially, the High Court was moved in an application under Section 482 of the CrPC, with a specific prayer for de-freezing of bank accounts. This application was withdrawn on 29 June 2016.
2. Subsequently, Criminal Application 459 of 2016 was lodged on 1 July 2016, soon after the earlier criminal application was dismissed as withdrawn, in order to assail the order of the Special Judge dated 1 July 2016, to allow the respondent to offer security of his immovable property in lieu of a cash deposit and for de-freezing his bank accounts.
3. The Single Judge of the Bombay High Court at its Nagpur Bench allowed the criminal application and issued a direction for the de-freezing of the respondent's bank accounts.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The appellant appealed to the Supreme Court against the judgment and order of the Single Judge of the Bombay High Court dated 18 August 2016. The Supreme Court allowed the appeal and set aside the impugned judgment and order of the learned Single Judge.

directions: The impugned judgment and order of the learned Single Judge dated 18 August 2016 is set aside.
Criminal application 459 of 2016 filed by the respondent before the Nagpur bench of the Bombay High Court shall stand dismissed.

issue.issue_text: Whether the filing of a subsequent application under Section 482 of the CrPC for the same relief that was previously withdrawn in an earlier application constitutes an abuse of the process of the court.

facts: The respondent filed an initial application (Criminal Application No 178 of 2016) under Section 482 of the CrPC before a Division Bench of the High Court.
This application included a specific prayer to de-freeze his bank accounts.
The respondent did not press this prayer and the application was disposed of as withdrawn on June 29, 2016.
Two days later, on July 1, 2016, the respondent filed a second application before a Single Judge of the same court, again seeking the de-freezing of his bank accounts.
The Single Judge was not informed that an earlier application seeking virtually the same relief had been withdrawn before the Division Bench.
law: The inherent powers of the High Court under Section 482 of the CrPC are to be exercised to prevent the abuse of the process of the court.
application: The Court found that the second application sought "virtually the same relief" as the first application that had been withdrawn.
By not pressing the prayer for de-freezing the accounts in the first application, the respondent had effectively given it up.

The act of filing another application for the same relief that had been previously abandoned, especially without disclosing the prior proceedings to the Single Judge, was deemed a "manifest abuse of process."
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court concluded that filing the second application for the same relief that had been given up in a prior withdrawn application was a manifest abuse of the process of the court. Therefore, the Single Judge ought not to have entertained the application.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the filing of a subsequent application under Section 482 of the CrPC for the same relief that was previously withdrawn in an earlier application constitutes an abuse of the process of the court.
appellant_arguments: The respondent engaged in a manifest abuse of the court's process.
The respondent had previously sought the specific relief of de-freezing accounts in an earlier criminal application.
Since that prayer was not pressed when the earlier application was withdrawn, it was an abuse of process to file a new application to seek and obtain the same relief before a different judge.
respondent_arguments: The respondent's arguments are not mentioned in the provided text.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: The court found it unnecessary to address the question of law adverted to by the High Court, and explicitly kept the question open.
obiter: The High Court was moved in an application under Section 482 of the CrPC, with a specific prayer for de-freezing.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The respondent had sought to de-freeze his bank accounts in an earlier criminal application. This prayer, together with the other reliefs (including that for quashing the FIR) was not pressed and the application was disposed of as withdrawn on 29 June 2016 by the Division Bench. In this background, the filing of another application before the Single Judge on 1 July 2016 for quashing the FIR and for de-freezing the bank accounts constituted a manifest abuse of process. The Single Judge was evidently not apprised of the fact that the earlier application seeking virtually the same relief had not been pressed before the division bench and had been withdrawn.
legal_tests_applied: Abuse of the process of the court
why_respondent_won: The respondent engaged in a manifest abuse of the court's process by filing a new application for the same relief that was previously withdrawn.
The respondent had specifically sought the relief of de-freezing his bank accounts in an earlier criminal application before a Division Bench.
The respondent did not press the prayer for de-freezing accounts when the earlier application was withdrawn.
It was an abuse of process to file a new application to seek and obtain the same relief before a different judge (a Single Judge).
The Single Judge was not informed that the earlier application seeking virtually the same relief had been withdrawn without being pressed.
policy_considerations: A litigant cannot be permitted to seek a specific relief, withdraw the application without pressing for that relief, and then file a new application for the same relief, as this constitutes a manifest abuse of the judicial process.
